assertions: Essex will take Reading: the town will be delivered to Parliament and will not be relieved or held for the King
The governor will capitulate and surrender the town on terms rather than hold it indefinitely or see Essex raise the siege
The taking will not be immediate or effortless: the Sun in a fixed sign in the 7th shows an obstinate defence first, with delay and hard pressure before surrender
The surrender will come within the present siege in April (month scale, late April) rather than after a prolonged months-long siege
Success brings honour to Essex: the Moon in the 10th near Regulus in mutual reception with Mars, his significator, fortifies his cause

The town is not taken simply by starvation: Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus placed therein for its ammunition and provision show supplies present, so delivery follows the governor's weakness (Saturn, lord of the 4th, in his fall) and military pressure, not immediate famine
summary: Essex will take Reading, by the governor's surrender after obstinate resistance, within this April siege.
method: Horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology, whole-sign classical rules)
reasoning: Scorpio ascending: Mars, lord of the Ascendant and significator of Essex, is well fortified apart from being in his fall and is in reception with the Moon (Mars in her house, she in his terms and face); Moon in the 10th near Regulus applies to Mars, giving Essex honour and eventual success, though the Moon void of course and the sextile counting as a square in signs of long ascension import difficulty and delay. The town is the 4th (Aquarius) and its governor Saturn, lord of the 4th, in his fall is too weak to hold. The King/garrison significator Sun in the 7th in a fixed sign explains stiff, obstinate resistance before delivery, not ultimate success. Jupiter/Venus for provision show the town is supplied, so the fall is by capitulation under pressure, not instant storm or famine. Timing scale is month: delivery in April of the siege.
